long_biography.plain_text:
Perkins grew up in a minister's family and earned money through odd jobs before settling in Tacoma as a travelling salesman. After a pharmaceutical-wholesale partnership failed, he repaid his debts and entered Republican Party organization, eventually becoming Senator Marcus Hanna's private secretary. With banker-backed credit but no inherited publishing assets, he bought the struggling Tacoma Evening News in 1898 and turned it into the base of a regional newspaper business.

He added the Tacoma Daily Ledger and acquired papers in Everett, Aberdeen, Bellingham and Olympia, creating the state's first newspaper chain under the Perkins Press name. Perkins sold his Tacoma titles in 1918 but retained The Olympian and Bellingham Herald through the rest of his life. His long public role also included leading the Washington State Historical Society and supporting Tacoma civic projects, while his newspaper company continued for more than a decade after his death.

The National Register, Tacoma archives and contemporary newspaper-trade coverage independently establish the same Tacoma publisher and Perkins Press career.

The authoritative vessel relationship is marked current from 2010 even though Perkins died in 1955 and historical evidence places his El Primero ownership from 1911. This impossible timing is treated as an upstream relationship artifact; it is not repeated in either biography or used to infer that Perkins owned the restored vessel after death.

Christian Lee Lint is a separate co-listed person associated with El Primero. No strong source reviewed here establishes a family, corporate, estate or transfer relationship between Lint and Perkins, so this dossier borrows no Lint facts and makes no claim about how the yacht reached any later owner.

HistoryLink reports a story that Perkins won El Primero in a game, but its exact game description differs from later retellings. Only documented ownership and the 1911 transfer are used for identity resolution; the anecdote is excluded from the biographies.

Self-made — independent start is supported unusually well: Perkins's father devoted his resources to church work, Perkins earned money through varied jobs, his first partnership failed, he repaid debts, and he lacked cash for his first newspaper. Banker Chester Thorne supplied commercial credit, which the taxonomy does not treat as inherited advantage.

Founder is used because Perkins created the Perkins Press platform and Washington's first newspaper chain, even though he assembled it by acquiring existing newspapers rather than launching each title. Acquirer and active publisher remain the more precise narrative mechanisms.

Media & Entertainment is used for both industry fields because newspaper publishing created the fortune and Perkins Press still operated two significant regional papers at his death. His mining interests, maritime company positions and political activity are documented but not shown to have displaced publishing as the principal wealth platform.
